tables.name: orders
tables.description: One row per order placed by a customer.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.doc: The customer who placed the order.

columns.name: status
columns.doc: Order state code: 1 = placed, 2 = shipped, 3 = returned.

columns.name: amount
columns.doc: Order value in US dollars, excluding tax.

questions.text: How many customers live in Haifa?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE city = 'Haifa'

questions.text: How many orders were sent back by customers?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 3

needs_docs.fact: code 3 means the order was returned

questions.text: What was the total order value in dollars during 2026?
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE ordered_on LIKE '2026%'

readings.sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY SUM(o.amount) DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Unless stated otherwise, the top customer means the one with the highest total order amount.
